1	# Coded Agents in Flow Projects (Sibling Folder)
2	
3	A coded agent can live as a sibling folder to a flow project inside the same solution. The flow references it via `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` with `section: "In this solution"`. The flow's `uip maestro flow registry list --local` discovers the agent by reading `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`, written by `uip solution project add`.
4	
5	For the published-agent path (deployed standalone via `uip codedagent deploy`), see [coded/flow-integration.md § Pattern 2](flow-integration.md#pattern-2-published-coded-agent).
6	
7	## Sibling Folder Structure
8	
9	The `<resourceKey>` is the local UUID minted by `uip solution project add` — stable the moment the agent joins the solution.
10	
11	```
12	<SolutionDir>/
13	├── <SolutionName>.uipx
14	├── resources/                      # created and maintained by `uip solution project add`
15	│   └── solution_folder/
16	│       ├── process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json   # holds the `resource.key` UUID
17	│       └── package/<CodedAgentProject>.json
18	├── <FlowProject>/
19	│   ├── <FlowName>.flow
20	│   └── project.uiproj
21	└── <CodedAgentProject>/
22	    ├── main.py                     # agent entrypoint
23	    ├── pyproject.toml              # Python project config
24	    ├── uipath.json                 # UiPath project config
25	    ├── entry-points.json           # generated by `uip codedagent init`
26	    ├── bindings.json               # runtime bindings
27	    ├── main.mermaid                # generated graph diagram
28	    ├── project.uiproj              # Studio Web project metadata
29	    ├── .env                        # environment variables
30	    ├── .uipath/
31	    │   └── telemetry.json          # telemetry config
32	    └── .venv/                      # local virtualenv (created by `uv sync`)
33	```
34	
35	### Key differences from a published coded agent
36	
37	- **`resource.key`** is minted locally at `uip solution project add` time, not by Orchestrator at `uip codedagent deploy` time
38	- **No `codedagent deploy`** — the agent ships inside the solution package
39	- **Registry discovery is `--local`** (reads `resources/solution_folder/process/` files); no login or `registry pull` required
40	- **`model.section`** is `"In this solution"`

42	## Scaffolding the Sibling-Folder Coded Agent
43	
44	The full end-to-end workflow (solution init → flow scaffold → agent scaffold → register → wire → validate) is owned by [`quickstart.md` § Scenario 2](quickstart.md#quick-start-scenario-2--in-solution-coded-agent-in-a-flow). This file covers the agent-side detail of step 3 (scaffold) and step 5 (registration) in finer detail; the canonical sequence stays in the quickstart so it remains executable in one pass.
45	
46	If the solution and flow project don't yet exist, run `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` and then `uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>"` from inside the solution **before** the steps below — those calls are the start of Scenario 2.
47	
48	1. From the solution directory, create the agent folder and scaffold inside it:
49	
50	   ```bash
51	   mkdir <CodedAgentProject>
52	   cd <CodedAgentProject>
53	   uv venv --python 3.13
54	   source .venv/bin/activate       # .venv/Scripts/activate on Windows
55	   uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>   # e.g. uipath for Coded Function
56	   uip codedagent setup --force
57	   uip codedagent new <agent-name>
58	   uv sync
59	   ```
60	
61	   For a simple stub with no LLM call, use the Coded Function framework
62	   (`uipath` package). This avoids downloading the full LangGraph or
63	   LlamaIndex stack and keeps the setup fast.
64	
65	2. Implement `main.py`. Use lazy LLM initialization (create clients inside functions, never at module level).
66	
67	3. Generate entry points:
68	
69	   ```bash
70	   uip codedagent init
71	   ```
72	
73	4. Register the agent in the solution — **this is the step that mints the `resource.key`** the flow will reference:
74	
75	   ```bash
76	   cd <SolutionDir>
77	   uip solution project add <CodedAgentProject> <SolutionName>.uipx --output json
78	   ```
79	
80	   After this command, `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json` holds the `resource.key` UUID.
81	
82	
83	### Flow Discovery
84	
85	From inside the flow project directory, the agent is discoverable via the in-solution registry. The `--local` flag tells the registry commands to walk up from CWD to find a `.uipx`, read the `resources/solution_folder/process/` files written by step 4, and surface every sibling project as a discoverable node type — all offline, without a tenant registry round-trip:
86	
87	```bash
88	# list every in-solution node type (all sibling projects)
89	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
90	
91	# fetch the full manifest for the coded agent
92	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json
93	```
94	
95	The second command's `Data.Node` object is what the flow skill pastes into the flow's `definitions[]`. For the node instance shape and top-level `bindings[]` entries, see [agent/impl.md § In-solution variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--in-solution-variant).
96	
97	Without `--local`, `registry list`/`get` query the tenant registry (Orchestrator-published resources only) and will not surface the sibling project.
98	
99	## Wiring the Agent's Inputs
100	
101	For inputs that reference flow variables, use `{ "type": "literal", "expression": "{{ $vars.X }}", "fieldType": "string" }` — NOT `=js:...` expressions. `=js:` ships as a literal string to the agent activity and fails at runtime with `Cannot find name '<identifier>'`.
102	
103	Input-only rule. Mapping the agent's output back to a flow-level global on an End node DOES use `=js:` — see [variables-and-expressions.md § Variable Updates](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md#variable-updates-variableupdates).

1	# Coded Agents — Flow Integration
2	
3	Coded agents in flows use the `uipath.core.agent.{key}` node with `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. Three patterns exist, distinguished by where the agent lives.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pattern 1: In-Solution Coded Agent
8	
9	The coded agent lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution as the flow. The flow references it with `section: "In this solution"`; the runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API.
10	
11	- **Agent-side scaffolding:** [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md)
12	- **Wiring the agent's inputs:** [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs)
13	- **Flow node JSON shape + top-level `bindings[]` + `definitions[]` entry:** [agent/impl.md § In-solution variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--in-solution-variant)
14	
15	The node-type's `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution project add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) and surfaced by `uip maestro flow registry list --local`.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Pattern 2: Published Coded Agent
20	
21	The coded agent is deployed to Orchestrator as a standalone tenant resource. Any solution can reference it.
22	
23	**When to use:** reused across flows, independent versioning, already deployed.
24	
25	```bash
26	uip codedagent deploy --my-workspace
27	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
28	```
29	
30	**Capture the package key from the deploy command's own output** — `uip codedagent deploy` prints JSON containing the package `Key` (an Orchestrator-assigned GUID). That GUID is the `resourceKey` used in the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey`. Always run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` after deploy to refresh the local flow registry cache, but do NOT depend on `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` to return the deployed agent — that search only enumerates built-in node types (`uipath.agent.autonomous`, etc.); user-deployed coded agents do not appear there, so an empty result is the *expected* state and is NOT a sign the deploy failed.
31	
32	Fallback discovery paths if the deploy output is unavailable or unparseable, **tried in order** — stop at the first one that returns the package:
33	
34	1. `uip or packages list --search "<agent-name>" --output json` (tenant feed listing). Returns 404 on tenants where the caller lacks `Orchestrator.Packages.View` scope — if so, move to (2).
35	2. `uip or processes list --folder-path "<FolderName>" --output json` if the agent was deployed via `--folder` rather than `--my-workspace`.
36	
37	If all paths return empty / 404, the deploy command's stdout JSON is authoritative — re-run the deploy and capture its output rather than chasing post-hoc discovery endpoints.
38	
39	For the flow node JSON shape, see [agent/impl.md § Published variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--published-variant). `model.section` is `"Published"`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Pattern 3: Tool Resource for Another Agent
44	
45	The coded agent is a tool that another agent (inline or published) can call. Requires deploying the coded agent to Orchestrator first.
46	
47	**Resource file** at `<AgentProject>/resources/<ResourceName>/resource.json`:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "$resourceType": "tool",
52	  "type": "agent",
53	  "name": "MyCodedAgent",
54	  "description": "What this agent does (shown to the parent LLM for tool selection)",
55	  "location": "external",
56	  "properties": {
57	    "processName": "<CODED_AGENT_PROCESS_NAME>",
58	    "folderPath": "<FOLDER_PATH>"
59	  },
60	  "inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": { "userInput": { "type": "string" } } },
61	  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content":   { "type": "string" } } },
62	  "id": "<UUID>",
63	  "referenceKey": ""
64	}
65	```
66	
67	Coded agents use `location: "external"`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Pattern Comparison
72	
73	| Aspect | In-Solution (1) | Published (2) | Tool (3) |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Node type | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (local, from `project add`) | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (Orchestrator-assigned) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` |
76	| Lifecycle | `uip solution upload` (single pass) | `uip codedagent deploy` | `uip codedagent deploy` |
77	| Runtime lookup | Studio Web projects API | Orchestrator Releases API | Orchestrator (via parent agent) |
78	| `model.section` | `"In this solution"` | `"Published"` or absent | n/a |
79	| Cross-flow reuse | No | Yes | Yes |
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Debug
84	
85	| Error | Cause | Fix |
86	| --- | --- | --- |
87	| Node doesn't resolve in SW (Pattern 1) | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (it matches `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) |
88	| Agent not found in registry (Pattern 2/3) | Not deployed or registry stale | `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
89	| Tool resource never called | Tool description too vague | Sharpen the `description` in `resource.json` |

24	## CLI Conventions
25	
26	| Command family | Accepts `--output json` |
27	|---|---|
28	| `uip login`, `uip login status`, `uip login tenant list`, `uip login tenant set`, `uip logout` | yes |
29	| `uip codedagent setup` | yes |
30	| `uip codedagent new`, `init`, `run`, `dev`, `eval`, `deploy`, `push`, `pull`, `invoke` | no (forwarded to the Python CLI) |
31	
32	Use `uip codedagent <cmd>`, not `uv run uipath <cmd>`. The wrapper injects session credentials (`UIPATH_URL`, `UIPATH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, org/tenant identifiers) from your `uip login` session into the Python subprocess; `uv run uipath` skips that injection.
33	
34	## Critical Rules
35	
36	- **NEVER add a `[build-system]` section to `pyproject.toml`**. No `hatchling`, no `setuptools`, no build backend. UiPath agents do not use a build system. Only include `[project]`, `[dependency-groups]`, and `[tool.*]` sections.
37	- **Always create a smoke evaluation set.** Every agent must include `evaluations/eval-sets/smoke-test.json` with 2-3 test cases covering the primary happy path (not exhaustive error-case coverage — the smoke set exists to catch regressions, not to fully validate behavior). Create it in the Evaluate step, not during Build.
38	- **Select a framework before writing any code.** If the prompt clearly implies a framework (e.g., mentions tools, RAG, multi-step orchestration, or a specific SDK), pick the best match. If the prompt is ambiguous, ask the user to choose from: Coded Function, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or OpenAI Agents.
39	- **Correct SDK import: `from uipath.platform import UiPath`** — not `from uipath import UiPath` (that path does not exist and will cause `ImportError`). Always instantiate `UiPath()` inside functions/nodes, never at module level.
40	- **Refresh the CLI's Python executable path after venv changes.** If `uip codedagent` reports that the UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or any error indicates a stale `uipathExePath`, activate the project venv and run `uip codedagent setup --force`. This rewrites the CLI configuration to point at the current `.venv` executable.
41	- **Auth check is one-shot.** Run `uip login status --output json` once, at step 5. If the user supplied environment + organization + tenant or explicitly asked to connect to a specific tenant, run the matching one-shot `uip login --organization "<ORG>" --tenant "<TENANT>" --output json` after the status check, even if another session is already logged in. Otherwise, the wrapper auto-refreshes tokens on subsequent cloud calls (no `uip login refresh` exists); re-auth only on a real `401`.
42	- **Use `uip codedagent run` from non-interactive shells.** `uip codedagent dev` auto-appends `--interactive`.
43	- **Runtime captures only the last node's delta as output.** `Annotated[list, operator.add]` reducers accumulate inside the graph but vanish from `--output-file` JSON and eval trajectories. Carry aggregate fields forward in each node's return (`{"items": [*state.get("items", []), x]}`) — see [frameworks/langgraph-integration.md](frameworks/langgraph-integration.md) § Runtime Output Quirk.
44	- **Verify the JSON, not the streamed display.** After `uip codedagent run --output-file out.json`, inspect `out.json` — the streamed view shows per-node deltas; the JSON is the runtime's actual final result. Mismatches expose the runtime quirk above.
45	- **Use `uip codedagent deploy` for packaging/publishing.** `uip codedagent pack` and `uip codedagent publish` are filtered by the wrapper.
46	- **NEVER run `uip login` without `--tenant`.** The interactive tenant picker does not work from Claude's Bash tool. Use the one-shot form `uip login --organization "<ORG>" --tenant "<TENANT>"`, mapping staging/alpha to `--authority` (see [../authentication.md](../authentication.md)).
47	- **Auth MUST be an interactive question only when needed and values are missing.** If the session check fails and the user did not provide all of environment / organization / tenant, your ENTIRE response must be a single direct question. Do NOT wrap it in bullet points, "Next Steps" headers, or status summaries. Just ask and stop:
48	
49	  > What is your UiPath **environment** (cloud/staging/alpha), **organization name**, and **tenant name**?
50	- **In a flow, coded agents are referenced via the [`agent`](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/) plugin** — node type `uipath.core.agent.{key}`, `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. See [flow-integration.md](flow-integration.md) for the three patterns: in-solution sibling folder, Orchestrator-published, tool resource.

75	## Quick Start: Scenario 1 — Standalone Coded Agent
76	
77	When the user asks to create and deploy an agent end-to-end, follow these steps in order. Skip stages that are already done.
78	
79	**IMPORTANT: Do NOT stop between steps to ask "would you like me to continue?" or list next steps. Execute the entire flow automatically.** Pause only when (a) you hit an **architectural fork** — a step with multiple valid implementations (framework choice, HITL pattern, evaluator type, deploy target, conversational vs not, etc.) — or (b) you need data only the user has (credentials, project ID). At a fork, apply **infer-or-ask**: if the prompt or context names the choice, infer it and continue; otherwise output ONLY the choice question as your entire response, then STOP and wait. For missing data, output ONLY the data request. After getting the answer, resume immediately. Forks for each step are documented in that step's referenced file — read the reference when you reach the step; do not guess.

81	Steps 8 and 9 are mandatory stops **for greenfield**: always ask the user, even if the user only said "build". They are **automatically resolved** for `local-workspace` (auto-sync) and for `existing-coded` with `has_project_id == true` (push) — see steps 8 and 9 for the branch logic.

83	1. **Framework** — **Skip if `framework != none`** (already chosen — verify the right `<framework>.json` is present and continue). Else select per the [Framework Selection](#framework-selection) section below.
84	2. **Setup** — Idempotent by `project_state` and `has_venv`:
85	   - `local-workspace` → Studio Web already scaffolded `pyproject.toml` / `<framework>.json` / `entry-points.json` / `bindings.json`. Run **only** the venv prep block when `has_venv == false`:
86	
87	     ```bash
88	     uv venv --python 3.13
89	     source .venv/bin/activate                 # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
90	     uv sync
91	     uip codedagent setup --force
92	     ```
93	
94	     If `has_venv == true`, just `source .venv/bin/activate` and continue. Do **not** run `uip codedagent new`. Re-run `init` only when schemas change — see step 6 for the full rule.
95	   - `existing-coded` → `source .venv/bin/activate`. If `has_venv == false`, run `uv venv --python 3.13 && source .venv/bin/activate && uv sync`. Then `uip codedagent setup --force` (idempotent — refreshes `uipathExePath`). Skip `uip codedagent new`. Run `uip codedagent init` only if `has_entry_points == false` or schemas changed.
96	   - `greenfield` → Full Workflow in [lifecycle/setup.md](lifecycle/setup.md). Infer the project name from the user's prompt or the current directory.
97	
98	   **Do NOT authenticate yet** — auth happens after build (step 5).
99	
100	   **Exception — Integration Service / SaaS-connector agents:** if the agent calls IS connector activities (`sdk.connections.invoke_activity`), you cannot author its `body_fields` / `ActivityMetadata` without `uip is resources describe` output, which is auth-gated. For these agents, do the step-5 auth one-shot **and** IS discovery (per [capabilities/integration-service.md](capabilities/integration-service.md) § Discovery) NOW, before Build, then resume at Build with the discovered metadata in hand. Non-IS agents keep the default order (auth after build).
101	3. **Build** — Implement agent logic using the selected framework's patterns. **For `local-workspace`: skip only the scaffold-cleanup sub-step below** — Studio Web supplied a clean shell, so the module-level-client checks aren't needed. Logic edits in `main.py` proceed normally. For `greenfield` / `existing-coded`, after scaffolding and before running `uip codedagent init`, inspect the generated code and clean up scaffold hazards:
102	   - No module-level `UiPathChat`, `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI`, `UiPath`, or other auth-dependent clients.
103	   - Instantiate LLM/SDK clients inside graph nodes/functions only.
104	   - Ensure importing `main.py` works without UiPath auth.
105	
106	   See [lifecycle/build.md](lifecycle/build.md) § Additional Instructions for the detailed Build-stage rules. After implementing, re-run `uip codedagent init` to update schemas from the actual code.
107	4. **Bindings** — Sync `bindings.json` with the code using [lifecycle/bindings-reference.md](lifecycle/bindings-reference.md).
108	5. **Auth (one-shot)** — Run `uip login status --output json` once. If the user supplied environment + organization + tenant, immediately run the matching one-shot login command from [../authentication.md](../authentication.md), using both `--organization` and `--tenant` in the same `uip login` command. Do this even when `Status: Logged in`, because the existing session may be for a different tenant. If no credentials were supplied and `Status: Logged in`, trust the wrapper for the rest of the run (it auto-refreshes tokens). Otherwise ask for credentials — output ONLY this question as your entire response:
109	
110	> What is your UiPath **environment** (cloud/staging/alpha), **organization name**, and **tenant name**?
111	
112	Then STOP and wait. On reply, run the matching one-shot login from [../authentication.md](../authentication.md) (maps environment → `--authority`). Never run `uip login` without `--tenant`.
113	6. **Run** — Re-run `uip codedagent init` first whenever any of these changed since the last init, **or** when `has_entry_points == false`:
114	   - `Input`/`Output`/`State` Pydantic models or TypedDicts — any field added, removed, renamed, or retyped counts (the class name being the same does not).
115	   - The entry function's signature (parameters or return type annotation).
116	   - `<framework>.json` (`langgraph.json` / `llama_index.json` / `openai_agents.json` / `uipath.json` `functions`).
117	
118	   Skip init only when the edit is purely inside node bodies / helpers (logic, prompts, business rules) and leaves every schema and the entry signature byte-identical. Then test locally with `uip codedagent run <ENTRYPOINT> '<input>'` (use the entrypoint name from `entry-points.json`, e.g., `main`).
119	7. **Evaluate** — Run `uip codedagent eval <ENTRYPOINT> evaluations/eval-sets/smoke-test.json --no-report`. Idempotent by `has_evaluators` / `has_smoke_set`: create the missing one(s) only — **never overwrite an existing evaluator config or smoke set**, the user may have tuned them.
120	
121	   **Default the smoke evaluator to an output-based type, never a trajectory or tool-call evaluator** (those score 0.0 on single-step agents — use them only for multi-step / tool-using agents). Pick:
122	
123	   - **Deterministic or structured output** (a fixed string, number, or JSON shape) → `uipath-exact-match`, `uipath-contains`, or `uipath-json-similarity`. No LLM, no tenant model needed, binary/continuous scoring. Prefer this whenever the task allows it.
124	   - **Natural-language output** (summaries, reports, free text) → `uipath-llm-judge-output-semantic-similarity` (`LLMJudgeOutputEvaluator`). Scores output semantics, works without tracing.

231	
232	Use when the coded agent is tightly coupled to one flow and lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution. The agent is wired to the flow via `--local` registry discovery — no separate Orchestrator deployment for the agent, no separate skill hand-off. **`uipath-agents` owns this scenario end-to-end** — solution scaffolding, flow scaffolding, agent build, registration, and flow wiring all happen here. Do not invoke `uipath-maestro-flow` as a separate skill; run the maestro-flow CLI commands directly from this workflow.
233	
234	Execute the following in order, end-to-end, in one pass — do not pause for confirmation between steps.

314	## Framework Selection
315	
316	> **First — is this an agent at all?** If the task is deterministic logic with no LLM reasoning (validate data, call an API with custom auth, transform records, upload/download files), it's a **Python Coded Function** — not an agent. Use the [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions) skill instead of this one. Coded Functions use typed I/O (`@dataclass`, Pydantic `BaseModel`, or a thin Python class with typed annotations) and a `functions` map in `uipath.json`; what distinguishes an agent is LLM reasoning and a framework graph.
317	
318	If the task needs LLM reasoning, infer the framework from the user's prompt when possible. If ambiguous, ask them to choose:
319	
320	1. **LangGraph** (recommended — best integrated with the UiPath ecosystem) — StateGraph with conditional routing, tool use, interrupts. Best for complex LLM agents.
321	2. **LlamaIndex** — Workflow with events and RAG support. Most complete LangGraph alternative.
322	3. **OpenAI Agents** — Lightweight agent with tools and handoffs. Best for simple LLM agents; lacks HITL, process invocation, and state persistence.
323	
324	**Inference hints:** mentions of tools/tool calling, multi-step, or orchestration → LangGraph. Simple handoffs or lightweight LLM → OpenAI Agents. No LLM needed → not an agent — use [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions). Summarize / research / synthesize over PDF or TXT (incl. bucket files, attachments) → not a framework choice — see [capabilities/deeprag/planning.md](capabilities/deeprag/planning.md). Per-row CSV extraction → see [capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md](capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md). When in doubt, ask.
325	
326	**Always tell the user which framework you selected and why** before proceeding to build. Example: "I'll use **LangGraph** for this agent since it involves tool calling and multi-step orchestration."

21	| Pattern | When to Use | Key Components |
22	|---------|-------------|----------------|

33	## Simple Direct Agent
34	
35	Minimal agent with synchronous or async logic, no LLM calls or external services. Best for deterministic transformations, calculations, and data processing.
36	
37	**When to use:** Pure computation, data validation, format conversion, rule-based decisions.
38	
39	```python
40	from pydantic import BaseModel
41	from uipath.tracing import traced
42	
43	class Input(BaseModel):
44	    a: float
45	    b: float
46	    operator: str
47	
48	class Output(BaseModel):
49	    result: float
50	
51	@traced(name="calculate", span_type="tool")
52	def calculate(operator: str, a: float, b: float) -> float:
53	    match operator:
54	        case "+": return a + b
55	        case "-": return a - b
56	        case "*": return a * b
57	        case "/": return a / b if b != 0 else 0.0
58	        case _: raise ValueError(f"Unknown operator: {operator}")
59	
60	@traced()
61	async def main(input: Input) -> Output:
62	    result = calculate(input.operator, input.a, input.b)
63	    return Output(result=result)
64	```
65	
66	**Key points:**
67	- `@traced()` on `main` is required for Orchestrator visibility
68	- Use `@traced(name=..., span_type="tool")` on helper functions for granular traces
69	- Use `@mockable` from `uipath.eval.mocks` on functions calling external services so evaluations can substitute example calls
70

73	## SDK Integration Agent
74	
75	Uses the `UiPath()` client to interact with platform services like assets, queues, jobs, and buckets.
76	
77	**When to use:** Reading/writing Orchestrator assets, managing queues, triggering processes, uploading attachments.
78	
79	```python
80	import os
81	from pydantic import BaseModel
82	from uipath.platform import UiPath
83	from uipath.tracing import traced
84	
85	class Input(BaseModel):
86	    asset_name: str
87	    folder_path: str
88	
89	class Output(BaseModel):
90	    value: str
91	    status: str
92	
93	@traced()
94	async def main(input: Input) -> Output:
95	    client = UiPath()
96	
97	    asset = client.assets.retrieve(
98	        name=input.asset_name,
99	        folder_path=input.folder_path,
100	    )
101	
102	    return Output(
103	        value=str(asset.value),
104	        status="retrieved",
105	    )
106	```
107	
108	**Key points:**
109	- `UiPath()` reads credentials from environment variables by default
110	- All services support `folder_path` and `folder_key` for folder targeting
111	- Every service method has an async variant with `_async` suffix
112	- See [SDK Services](../capabilities/sdk-services.md) for the full API reference

116	## LangGraph Workflow Agent
117	
118	Multi-step agent using LangGraph's `StateGraph` with nodes, edges, and conditional routing. Supports LLM-powered decisions.
119	
120	> **Important:** LangGraph agents require `uipath-langchain` as a dependency and use a different project structure than coded function agents. See the LangGraph integration reference for project setup, `langgraph.json` configuration, and troubleshooting.
121	
122	**When to use:** Classification workflows, multi-step reasoning, conditional branching based on LLM output.
123	
124	```python
125	from pydantic import BaseModel
126	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph, MessagesState
127	from langgraph.types import Command
128	from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage
129	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
130	
131	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
132	    message: str
133	
134	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
135	    label: str
136	    confidence: float
137	
138	class GraphState(MessagesState):
139	    message: str
140	    label: str | None = None
141	    confidence: float | None = None
142	
143	async def classify(state: GraphState) -> Command:
144	    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(max_retries=3)
145	    result = await llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
146	    return Command(update={"label": "urgent", "confidence": 0.95})
147	
148	def route(state: GraphState) -> str:
149	    if (state.get("confidence") or 0) >= 0.8:
150	        return END
151	    return "review"
152	
153	builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
154	builder.add_node("classify", classify)
155	builder.add_edge(START, "classify")
156	builder.add_conditional_edges("classify", route)
157	graph = builder.compile()
158	```
159	
160	**Key points:**
161	- Use `MessagesState` for agents that need conversation history
162	- `Command(update={...})` to update state from nodes
163	- Conditional edges for routing based on state values
164	- LangGraph agents get tracing automatically — no `@traced()` needed on graph nodes
165

168	## Human-in-the-Loop Agent
169	
170	Extends a LangGraph workflow with `interrupt()` to pause execution and create an Action Center task for human review.
171	
172	**When to use:** Approval workflows, escalation paths, human review of LLM output, compliance checks.
173	
174	```python
175	from pydantic import BaseModel
176	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph, MessagesState
177	from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver
178	from langgraph.types import interrupt, Command
179	from uipath.platform.common import CreateTask
180	
181	class GraphState(MessagesState):
182	    label: str | None = None
183	    approved: bool = False
184	
185	async def wait_for_human(state: GraphState) -> Command:
186	    action_data = interrupt(
187	        CreateTask(
188	            app_name="review_app",
189	            app_folder_path="MyFolderPath",
190	            title="Review classification result",
191	            data={"label": state["label"]},
192	            assignee="reviewer@company.com",
193	        )
194	    )
195	    approved = isinstance(action_data.get("Answer"), bool) and action_data["Answer"]
196	    return Command(update={"approved": approved})
197	
198	def route_after_review(state: GraphState) -> str:
199	    return END if state["approved"] else "escalate"
200	
201	builder = StateGraph(GraphState)
202	builder.add_node("classify", classify_node)
203	builder.add_node("human_review", wait_for_human)
204	builder.add_node("escalate", escalate_node)
205	builder.add_edge(START, "classify")
206	builder.add_edge("classify", "human_review")
207	builder.add_conditional_edges("human_review", route_after_review)
208	graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())
209	```
210	
211	**Key points:**
212	- `interrupt()` pauses the graph and creates an Action Center task via `CreateTask`
213	- A `checkpointer` (e.g., `MemorySaver()`) is required for interrupt/resume to work
214	- `CreateTask` fields: `app_name`, `app_folder_path`, `title`, `data` (dict shown to reviewer), `assignee` (optional)
215	- Dynamic app folder paths require manual binding.
216	- The graph resumes when the human completes the action — return value comes from `interrupt()`

220	## RAG Agent
221	
222	Retrieval-Augmented Generation using UiPath Context Grounding as a vector store with an LLM for answer synthesis.
223	
224	**When to use:** Knowledge base Q&A, document search, grounded answers with source citations.
225	
226	```python
227	from pydantic import BaseModel
228	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
229	from uipath_langchain.vectorstores.context_grounding_vectorstore import (
230	    ContextGroundingVectorStore,
231	)
232	from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
233	from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
234	from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough
235	
236	class Input(BaseModel):
237	    query: str
238	    index_name: str
239	    k: int = 3
240	
241	class Output(BaseModel):
242	    answer: str
243	    sources: list[str]
244	
245	async def main(input: Input) -> Output:
246	    vectorstore = ContextGroundingVectorStore(index_name=input.index_name)
247	    retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": input.k})
248	
249	    prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
250	        "Answer based on this context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"
251	    )
252	    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(max_retries=3)
253	
254	    chain = (
255	        {"context": retriever, "question": RunnablePassthrough()}
256	        | prompt
257	        | llm
258	        | StrOutputParser()
259	    )
260	
261	    docs = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search_with_score(
262	        query=input.query, k=input.k
263	    )
264	    answer = await chain.ainvoke(input.query)
265	
266	    return Output(
267	        answer=answer,
268	        sources=[doc.metadata.get("source", "") for doc, _ in docs],
269	    )
270	```
271	
272	**Key points:**
273	- `ContextGroundingVectorStore` connects to UiPath Context Grounding indexes
274	- Use `.as_retriever()` to integrate with LangChain's LCEL chains
275	- `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` routes through UiPath's LLM Gateway
276	- Supports both sync (`invoke`) and async (`ainvoke`) retrieval
277	
278	---
279	
280	## Chat Agent
281	
282	Conversational agent with tool access, built using LangGraph's `create_react_agent()` helper. Minimal boilerplate for tool-using chat agents.
283	
284	**When to use:** Conversational assistants, tool-augmented chat, agents that need web search or API access.
285	
286	```python
287	from pydantic import BaseModel
288	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
289	from langchain_tavily import TavilySearch
290	from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
291	
292	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
293	    question: str
294	
295	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
296	    answer: str
297	
298	system_prompt = """You are a helpful assistant that answers questions.
299	Use the search tool to find current information when needed."""
300	
301	def build_graph():
302	    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
303	    tools = [TavilySearch(max_results=3)]
304	    return create_react_agent(llm, tools=tools, prompt=system_prompt)
305	```
306	
307	**Key points:**
308	- `create_react_agent()` handles the agent loop (reason → act → observe) automatically
309	- Pass any LangChain-compatible tools in the `tools` list
310	- The `prompt` parameter guides agent behavior and tool usage
311	- Supports any LangChain chat model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, etc.)
312	
313	---
314	
315	## Multi-Agent Supervisor
316	
317	A supervisor agent routes tasks to specialized worker agents, then synthesizes results. Each worker is an independent agent with its own tools and prompt.
318	
319	**When to use:** Complex tasks requiring different expertise, divide-and-conquer workflows, research + code generation.
320	
321	```python
322	from typing import Literal
323	from pydantic import BaseModel
324	from typing_extensions import TypedDict
325	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph, MessagesState
326	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
327	from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
328	from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
329	
330	members = ["researcher", "coder"]
331	options = members + ["FINISH"]
332	
333	class Router(TypedDict):
334	    next: str  # One of: "researcher", "coder", "FINISH"
335	
336	class State(MessagesState):
337	    next: str
338	    answer: str
339	
340	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
341	    question: str
342	
343	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
344	    answer: str
345	
346	def make_supervisor(llm):
347	    router_llm = llm.with_structured_output(Router)
348	    async def supervisor(state: State) -> dict:
349	        response = await router_llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
350	        return {"next": response["next"]}
351	    return supervisor
352	
353	_agents = None
354	
355	def get_agents():
356	    global _agents
357	    if _agents is not None:
358	        return _agents
359	    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
360	    _agents = (
361	        create_react_agent(llm, tools=[search_tool], prompt="You research."),
362	        create_react_agent(llm, tools=[repl_tool], prompt="You write code."),
363	        llm,
364	    )
365	    return _agents
366	
367	async def research_node(state: State):
368	    research_agent, _, _ = get_agents()
369	    result = await research_agent.ainvoke(state)
370	    return {"messages": [HumanMessage(content=result["messages"][-1].content, name="researcher")]}
371	
372	async def code_node(state: State):
373	    _, code_agent, _ = get_agents()
374	    result = await code_agent.ainvoke(state)
375	    return {"messages": [HumanMessage(content=result["messages"][-1].content, name="coder")]}
376	
377	async def supervisor_node(state: State):
378	    _, _, supervisor_llm = get_agents()
379	    return await make_supervisor(supervisor_llm)(state)
380	
381	def route_supervisor(state: State) -> str:
382	    match state.get("next", "FINISH"):
383	        case "researcher": return "researcher"
384	        case "coder": return "coder"
385	        case _: return END
386	
387	builder = StateGraph(State, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
388	builder.add_node("supervisor", supervisor_node)
389	builder.add_node("researcher", research_node)
390	builder.add_node("coder", code_node)
391	builder.add_edge(START, "supervisor")
392	builder.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", route_supervisor)
393	builder.add_edge("researcher", "supervisor")
394	builder.add_edge("coder", "supervisor")
395	graph = builder.compile()
396	```
397	
398	**Key points:**
399	- The supervisor uses `with_structured_output(Router)` to decide which worker to call
400	- Workers return results as `HumanMessage` with a `name` so the supervisor can track who responded
401	- Workers loop back to the supervisor, which decides the next step or finishes
402	- Each worker is a full `create_react_agent()` with its own tools and prompt
403	
404	---
405	
406	## Common Building Blocks
407	
408	- **Pydantic models** — Every agent defines `Input`/`Output` (or `GraphInput`/`GraphOutput`) as `BaseModel` subclasses. Run `uip codedagent init` after changing them.
409	- **`@traced()`** — Apply to `main` and key helpers. LangGraph agents get tracing automatically.
410	- **`@mockable`** — From `uipath.eval.mocks`. Wrap functions calling external services so evaluations can return `ExampleCall` outputs without hitting the network.
411	- **Async** — All patterns support `async def main(...)`. SDK methods have `_async` variants.

1	# Setup UiPath Agent Project
2	
3	## Preflight
4	
5	```bash
6	python --version                                           # 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13
7	which uv  > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "install uv:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh"
8	which uip > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "install uip: npm install -g @uipath/cli"
9	```
10	
11	## Framework Selection
12	
13	Pick the framework before starting. The package installed in the Workflow determines which scaffold `uip codedagent new` produces.
14	
15	| Agent Type | `<FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>` | Framework config | Guide |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| Coded Function | `uipath` | `uipath.json` | [coded-function-agents.md](../frameworks/coded-function-agents.md) |
18	| LangGraph | `"uipath-langchain"` | `langgraph.json` | [langgraph-integration.md](../frameworks/langgraph-integration.md) |
19	| LlamaIndex | `uipath-llamaindex` | `llama_index.json` | [llamaindex-integration.md](../frameworks/llamaindex-integration.md) |
20	| OpenAI Agents | `uipath-openai-agents` | `openai_agents.json` | [openai-agents-integration.md](../frameworks/openai-agents-integration.md) |
21	
22	## Starting Points
23	
24	| Starting from | Use |
25	|---|---|
26	| Empty directory | The Workflow below |
27	| Existing UiPath agent (has `main.py` + `<framework>.json` + UiPath deps) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` only |
28	| Existing Python agent (has `main.py`, missing UiPath deps / framework config) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, `uv add <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>`, adapt `main.py` per the framework guide, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` |
29	| Studio Web Local Workspace solution (ancestor contains `.sw-path-marker` or `.local/folder.lock`) | Already scaffolded by Studio Web. One-time local-run prep: `uv venv --python 3.13`, activate, `uv sync`, `uip codedagent setup --force`. Do **not** run `uip codedagent new`. Re-run `init` after every edit that adds/removes/renames/retypes a field on `Input`/`Output`/`State` or changes the entry-function signature — see [local-workspace.md](local-workspace.md) § Schema Sync After Edits for the full rule and anti-patterns. |
30	
31	## Workflow
32	
33	```bash
34	mkdir <PROJECT_NAME> && cd <PROJECT_NAME>
35	uv venv --python 3.13                        # uv defaults to the latest Python; pin to a UiPath-supported version
36	source .venv/bin/activate                    # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
37	uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>
38	uip codedagent setup --force
39	uip codedagent new <PROJECT_NAME>
40	uv add uipath-dev --dev                      # required by `uip codedagent dev` (local dev web server)
41	uv sync
42	uip codedagent init
43	```
44	
45	`uipath-dev` is added to the dev dependency group during scaffold so `uip codedagent dev` works later without a second install pass. Skipping it causes `uip codedagent dev` to fail with *"The 'uipath-dev' package is required to use the dev command"*.
46	
47	**What `uip codedagent setup` does:** locates a Python that has `uipath` installed and caches its path, so later commands (`init`/`run`/`eval`/`pack`) can invoke the Python SDK. It searches PATH (`python3.x`, `python3`, `python`) and uses your `.venv` only when activated. So when using uv, always `uv sync` then activate the venv before the `setup` command.
48	
49	## Coded Function Agents
50	
51	`uipath.json` carries the entrypoint mapping:
52	
53	```json
54	{
55	  "functions": {
56	    "main": "main.py:main"
57	  }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	Edit the scaffolded `main.py`'s `Input` / `Output` models and `async def main` to fit the real agent.
62	
63	## Generated Files
64	
65	| File | Purpose |
66	|---|---|
67	| `pyproject.toml` | Project metadata and dependencies |
68	| `main.py` | Agent entrypoint |
69	| `<framework>.json` | Framework config (LangGraph / LlamaIndex / OpenAI Agents) |
70	| `uipath.json` | Runtime options, pack options, `functions` map |
71	| `entry-points.json` | Input / output schemas from Pydantic models |
72	| `bindings.json` | Runtime bindings |
73	| `uv.lock` | Dependency lockfile |
74	| `.uipath/telemetry.json` | Telemetry configuration |
75	| `AGENTS.md`, `.agent/` | Documentation |
76	
77	## `uipath.json`
78	
79	```json
80	{
81	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
82	  "runtimeOptions": {
83	    "isConversational": false
84	  },
85	  "packOptions": {
86	    "fileExtensionsIncluded": [],
87	    "filesIncluded": [],
88	    "filesExcluded": [],
89	    "directoriesExcluded": [],
90	    "includeUvLock": true
91	  },
92	  "functions": {}
93	}
94	```
95	
96	**Key fields:**
97	- **`runtimeOptions.isConversational`** - scaffold defaults to `false` (single-shot). Building a chat/conversational agent? Flip to `true` BEFORE `uip codedagent init` so `entry-points.json` gets the chat shape. See [conversational-agents](../capabilities/conversational-agents.md).
98	- **`packOptions`** - Control which files are included when packaging for deployment
99	- **`functions`** - Entrypoint mappings (format: `"file_path:function_name"`)
100	
101	### `packOptions.directoriesExcluded` for solution context
102	
103	When the agent project is registered in a solution and uploaded via `uip solution upload`, the agent directory is bundled into the solution archive. Set `directoriesExcluded` to keep Python build artifacts out of the archive:
104	
105	```json
106	"packOptions": {
107	  "directoriesExcluded": [".venv", "__pycache__"],
108	  "includeUvLock": true
109	}
110	```
111	
112	`.venv/` is hundreds of MB of installed wheels and breaks uploads. `__pycache__/` is ephemeral bytecode. Both regenerate from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` on the target side. Without these exclusions, `uip solution upload` produces an oversized archive that can be rejected by Studio Web.
113	
114	- `isConversational: true` for chat-style agents.
115	- `packOptions` controls `.nupkg` contents at deploy time.
116	
117	## Troubleshooting
118	
119	| Error | Cause | Fix |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| `uipath executable not found` | `setup` not run, or run without venv activated | Activate `.venv` and re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
122	| UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or `uipathExePath` is stale | The CLI still points at an old or missing virtualenv executable | Run `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force` to refresh `uipathExePath` |
123	| `Found .venv in current directory but no virtual environment is activated` | `.venv` exists but `VIRTUAL_ENV` is unset | Activate `.venv` first, then re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
124	| `No compatible Python installation found` | Python outside 3.11 – 3.13 | Install 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13 (or set `PYTHON_TOOL_PYTHON_VERSIONS`) |
125	| `Project authors cannot be empty` | Missing `authors` in `pyproject.toml` | Add `authors = [{ name = "Your Name" }]` to `[project]` |
126	| `NameError` during `init` | Framework not installed when `init` imports `main.py` | Run `uv sync` before `uip codedagent init` |
127	| `No entrypoints found in uipath.json` | Framework config or package missing | Verify `uv pip install` succeeded, then re-run `uip codedagent init` |
128	| `ModuleNotFoundError` for a package you just installed, even after activating `.venv` | A shell `python` alias points at a different interpreter (uv-managed, system, etc.) | Use `.venv/bin/python` directly for sanity checks, or `unalias python` for the session |

28	## Framework Reference
29	
30	| Framework | Config File | Key Dependency | Entry Point |
31	|-----------|------------|----------------|-------------|
32	| Coded Function | `uipath.json` | `uipath` | `main.py` function |
33	| LangGraph | `langgraph.json` | `uipath-langchain` | `main.py` compiled StateGraph |
34	| LlamaIndex | `llama_index.json` | `uipath-llamaindex` | `main.py` Workflow instance |
35	| OpenAI Agents | `openai_agents.json` | `uipath-openai-agents` | `main.py` Agent instance |
36	
37	## Troubleshooting
38	
39	| Error | Cause | Solution |
40	|-------|-------|----------|
41	| `'dict' has no attribute '...'` | `with_structured_output()` returns a dict, not a Pydantic model | Access results with `result['key']` dict syntax, not `result.key` attribute access |
42	| `ImportError: Could not import <package>` | External tool package not in `pyproject.toml` | Add all third-party tool packages to dependencies: `uv add <package>` |
43	| Agent returns empty output | Entry point not wired correctly | Verify `main.py` exports the correct object (compiled graph, Workflow, Agent) |
44	| `TypeError` on Input/Output | Schema mismatch after code change | Re-run `uip codedagent init` to regenerate `entry-points.json` |
45	
46	## Additional Instructions
47	
48	- **File/document input → `Attachment`, never a filesystem path string.** If the prompt says the agent "takes a CSV/PDF/file as input" (or similar), read `../capabilities/file-attachments.md` before defining the `Input` model. A `str` path field runs locally with `uip codedagent run` but breaks on Studio Web/Orchestrator, where no such path exists in the container.
49	- **Select a framework before writing any code.** Infer from the prompt if possible (tools/orchestration → LangGraph, RAG → LlamaIndex, simple LLM → OpenAI Agents, no LLM → Coded Function). If ambiguous, ask the user to choose.
50	- **Structured input contract → not OpenAI Agents.** OpenAI Agents always require a `messages` input field and cannot express an input contract without it (see `../frameworks/openai-agents-integration.md` § Input). When the user needs a strict typed/structured input (e.g. a single named field, no `messages`), choose LangGraph (custom `StateGraph` with arbitrary input state) instead. Do NOT silently fall back to a Coded Function to satisfy the input shape — a Coded Function produces `ProjectType: Function`, not a coded agent, so it does not fulfill a request for an agent.
51	- **Read ONLY the single framework reference** for the selected framework before writing code. Do NOT read other framework references or capability references unless the task explicitly requires that capability.
52	- **Clean generated scaffold code before schema init.** After `uip codedagent new` and before running `uip codedagent init`, inspect `main.py` and remove scaffold hazards: no module-level `UiPathChat`, `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI`, `UiPath`, or other auth-dependent clients; instantiate LLM/SDK clients inside graph nodes/functions only; ensure importing `main.py` works without UiPath auth.
53	- **NEVER instantiate LLM clients or SDK clients at module level.** `uip codedagent init` imports your Python file to introspect schemas — module-level `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()`, `UiPathChat()`, `UiPathChatOpenAI()`, or `UiPath()` will fail because auth may not have happened yet. Always create these instances inside functions or graph nodes, never at the top level of the module.
54	- **Correct SDK import: `from uipath.platform import UiPath`** — not `from uipath import UiPath` (that does not exist). Instantiate inside functions only: `sdk = UiPath()`.
55	- LangGraph agents get tracing automatically — no `@traced()` needed on graph nodes.
56	- Simple function agents require `@traced()` on the `main` function.

1	# Coded vs Low-Code Agent Selection Guide
2	
3	Reference for comparing **coded** (Python) and **low-code** (agent.json) agents. Use this when the user needs help deciding which mode to choose.
4	
5	## Capability Matrix
6	
7	| Capability | Low-code | Coded |
8	|---|:---:|:---:|
9	| Build without writing Python | ✅ | ❌ |
10	| Call UiPath processes / API workflows as tools | ✅ | ✅ |
11	| Use Integration Service connectors | ✅ | ✅ |
12	| RAG over Context Grounding index | ✅ | ✅ |
13	| Use third-party Python libraries | ❌ | ✅ |
14	| Custom LLM state machine (LangGraph StateGraph) | ❌ | ✅ |
15	| Human-in-the-loop | ✅ escalation | ✅ `interrupt()` |
16	| Complex conditional HITL resume logic | ❌ | ✅ |
17	| Studio Web Agent Builder canvas | ✅ | Optional |
18	| `@mockable` for evaluation isolation | ❌ | ✅ |
19	| Full runtime control over LLM prompts | ❌ | ✅ |
20	| Multi-model / multi-framework strategies | ❌ | ✅ |
21	| Fastest path to first working agent | ✅ | ❌ |
22	| Conversational (chat-style, multi-turn) use-cases | ✅ | currently not recommended for production, use low-code |
23	| Embed inline in a flow project | ✅ | ❌ |
24	| Embed as sibling project in same solution | ✅ | ✅ |
25	| Invoke as published agent node in a flow | ✅ | ✅ |
26	| Use as tool resource for another agent in a flow | ✅ | ✅ |
27	| Solution-level deployment with resource provisioning | ✅ | ❌ |
28	
29	## Key Differences
30	
31	| Aspect | Coded | Low-code |
32	|--------|-------|----------|
33	| Language | Python | Declarative JSON (`agent.json`) |
34	| CLI | `uip codedagent` | `uip agent` + `uip solution` |
35	| Project marker | `pyproject.toml` + `.py` files | `agent.json` + `project.uiproj` |
36	| Frameworks | LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents, Coded Function | None (prompt + tools config) |
37	| Deployment | `uip codedagent deploy` | `uip solution pack/publish/deploy` |
38	| Local testing | `uip codedagent run` | Studio Web only |
39	| Evaluations | `uip codedagent eval` (13 evaluator types) | Not available |
40	| Flow integration | Inline, published node, tool resource (3 patterns) | Inline, published, solution, external, tool resource (5 patterns) |
41	| Solution support | Standalone projects | Full solution lifecycle |
42	| Custom code | Full Python | None |
43	| Sync | `uip codedagent push/pull` | `uip solution upload` |
44	
45	## Solution-Level Mixing
46	
47	A UiPath solution can contain **both** coded and low-code agent projects. Each project is independently one mode or the other — there is no hybrid within a single project.
48	
49	### Pattern 1: Low-code orchestrator calling coded agent as tool
50	
51	The low-code agent adds the coded agent as an **external tool** in its `resources[]` array:
52	
53	```jsonc
54	{
55	  "$resourceType": "tool",
56	  "type": "agent",
57	  "location": "external",
58	  "properties": {
59	    "processName": "MyCodedAgent",
60	    "folderPath": "Shared/CodedAgents"
61	  }
62	}
63	```
64	
65	The coded agent must be deployed to Orchestrator first via `uip codedagent deploy`.
66	
67	### Pattern 2: Coded agent invoking low-code agent via SDK
68	
69	The coded agent calls the deployed low-code agent as an Orchestrator process:
70	
71	```python
72	sdk = UiPath()
73	result = await sdk.processes.invoke(
74	    name="MySolution.agent.MyLowCodeAgent",
75	    folder_path="Shared/MySolution",
76	    input_arguments={"userInput": "Hello"}
77	)
78	```
79	
80	The low-code agent must be deployed via `uip solution deploy` first.
81	
82	### Pattern 3: Mixed solution
83	
84	A solution contains both project types, deployed together:
85	
86	```
87	MySolution/
88	├── LowCodeAgent/      ← agent.json (low-code)
89	├── CodedAgent/        ← pyproject.toml + .py (coded)
90	├── resources/
91	└── MySolution.uipx
92	```
93	
94	Each agent type uses its own CLI and lifecycle. The solution's `uip solution deploy` handles both.
95	
96	## Interop Mechanisms
97	
98	| From | To | Mechanism |
99	|------|----|-----------|
100	| Low-code | Coded (deployed) | Agent tool resource with `location: "external"` in `agent.json` |
101	| Coded | Low-code (deployed) | `sdk.processes.invoke()` targeting the deployed agent process |
102	| Low-code | Low-code (same solution) | Agent tool resource with `location: "solution"` in `agent.json` |
103	| Low-code | Low-code (different solution) | Agent tool resource with `location: "external"` in `agent.json` |
104	| Coded | Coded | `workflows.*` or `sdk.processes.invoke()` |
105	| Flow | Coded (deployed) | Published agent node (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`) in the flow |
106	| Flow | Low-code (deployed) | Published agent node (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`) in the flow |
107	| Flow (inline low-code agent) | Coded (deployed) | Tool resource (`uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent`) wired to the agent |
108	
109	### Flow Integration Details
110	
111	- **Low-code agents** support 5 Flow patterns: inline embedding, published node, solution-level, external, and tool resource
112	- **Coded agents** support 3 Flow patterns: in-solution sibling project (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` with `section: "In this solution"`), published node (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` via `uip codedagent deploy`), and tool resource
113	- **Low-code inline embedding**: `uip agent init --inline-in-flow` creates a `<projectId-uuid>` subdirectory inside the flow project
114	- **Coded solution-level embedding**: The coded agent lives as a sibling folder to the flow project; `uip solution project add` mints the `resource.key` that the flow's `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` node references, discoverable via `uip maestro flow registry list --local` (see [coded/embedding-in-flows.md](coded/embedding-in-flows.md))
115	- Node types differ by pattern: inline low-code uses `uipath.agent.autonomous`; every other case (published low-code, in-solution coded, published coded) uses `uipath.core.agent.{key}`
116	- For coded agent Flow integration details, see [coded/flow-integration.md](coded/flow-integration.md)
117

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
52	
53	## Project structure (generated scaffold)
54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
63	```
64	
65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.
247	
248	## Definition entry
249	
250	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
251	
252	```bash
253	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
254	```
255	
256	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array.
